posted.message: This change removes the previously exported `prerender` and `prerenderToNodeStream` symbols and only re-exports `unstable_prerenderToNodeStream`. In a 19.1.x patch release, dropping existing exports is a runtime breaking change for consumers importing the old names. If this was intended, consider keeping backward-compatible aliases (or guarded exports) for the old API names.

title: ♻️ Do not accept underscore headers when using `convert_underscores=True` (the default)

posted.message: `processed_keys.add(get_validation_alias(field))` is applied unconditionally for all parameter sources, but the stated intent is specific to headers with `convert_underscores=True`. This may change extra-param handling for non-header params (or other alias configurations) by marking additional keys as processed and preventing them from being treated as extras. Should this be gated to header params (and only when underscore conversion is enabled) to avoid behavior changes outside headers?

posted.message: This assumes `HttpsProxyAgent` exposes a callable instance property `callback`. In newer `https-proxy-agent`/`agent-base` variants the hook is `connect(...)` (or otherwise not exposed as `callback`), so `const callback = agent.callback` can be `undefined` and `callback.call(...)` will throw at runtime for proxied HTTPS requests. Consider feature-detecting the hook (`callback` vs `connect`) or applying TLS option merging via a supported extension point instead of patching a private/internal property.

posted.message: `beforeRedirectAuth` depends entirely on `redirectOptions.href` being present (`new URL(redirectOptions.href)`). If `follow-redirects` ever invokes `beforeRedirect` with only component fields (`protocol`/`hostname`/`path`) or a relative target without `href`, this throws and is silently ignored, causing auth to be dropped even on same-origin redirects. Consider deriving the redirect URL from available option fields when `href` is missing, rather than fail-open to stripping in all such cases.
